reference.notes:
`parseURL` now removes the slash in front of a Windows drive letter (`/C:` → `C:`) only when the protocol is exactly `file:` as written in the input. The whole suite passes, including both new suites: 652 tests with type checking and no type errors. ESLint and Prettier also pass on `src`.

The fix is one line in `src/parse.ts:74`. The existing pattern `/\/(?=[A-Za-z]:)/` is now applied only when `protocol === "file:"`; for any other protocol, or none, the path goes to `parsePath` unchanged. The pattern is still unanchored and removes only the first match. The check is case-sensitive, so `FILE:///C:/foo` keeps `/C:/foo`, though the protocol returned is still lowercased. `defaultProto` only counts once it has been added to the front of the input, as before. No exports or signatures changed.

`src/parse.ts` had no function bodies throwing `not implemented`. It still had the old behaviour, so I edited the existing code instead.
